title: API: MetadataBackend::create_object id-must-be-set invariant is documented but unenforced
description:
backend.rs:64-70 — create_object's rustdoc states:

  '# Invariant
  The returned O MUST have its id field set to the server-assigned Id returned as the first element of the tuple. The handler relies on this to populate the created response map per RFC 8620 §5.3.'

The handler at metadata.rs:324-330 then does:

    Ok((_new_id, created_obj)) => {
        mutated = true;
        created.insert(
            create_id,
            serde_json::to_value(&created_obj)
                .expect('derive(Serialize) on plain data is infallible'),
        );
    }

The handler discards _new_id (the first tuple element) and serializes only created_obj. A buggy backend that returns (assigned_id, an_object_with_id_field_None_or_wrong) produces a created map entry whose 'id' is null or wrong, and the wire response silently misleads the client (RFC 8620 §5.3 requires the response to include the server-assigned id in created[create_id].id).

Two failure modes left to backend authors to avoid via discipline:
1. Backend returns Ok((id, obj)) with obj.id = None — wire response has 'id': null.
2. Backend returns Ok((id, obj)) with obj.id = Some(different_id) — wire response has a wrong id, silently inconsistent with the state the backend stored under 'id'.

Recommendation:
- Either tighten the handler to inject _new_id into created_obj before serialization (canonical cookie-cut pattern from jmap-mail-server's analogous handler — verify the mail-server handler also has this gap or already has the injection), OR add a debug_assert!(created_obj.id() == Some(&new_id)) that catches the contract violation in dev builds, OR strengthen the trait method signature to return Result<(Id, O), _> where O is guaranteed to carry the id (e.g. return only the JSON Value with the id field already injected, like the canonical MockBackend already does at lib.rs:408-411 in this crate).

What goes wrong if this stays:
- Backend bugs surface as silently-wrong wire responses (`id: null`) rather than as either a Rust-side panic or a serverFail. The 'plain data Serialize is infallible' expect at metadata.rs:329 documents that the JSON construction cannot fail — but says nothing about whether the resulting JSON is correct.

Caller test discipline alone cannot guard against this: the in-tree integration tests at tests/metadata_tests.rs use MemoryBackend which DOES correctly inject the id (memory.rs:632), so the contract violation is invisible to anyone copying the test layout.
close_reason: moot: MetadataBackend and create_object removed in b34a07bf (crate-jmap-metadata-server/src/lib.rs:30-37)
